newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical gets 14.9 pct Circon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical gets 14.9 pct Circon.

text.p: United States Surgical Corp said Tuesday it bought 973,174 more shares of Circon Corp, and now owns a 14.9 percent stake in the company.
The company completed on July 14 a tender offer for the Circon stock at $14.50 per share. About 4.508 million shares were tendered.
Of that total number of shares tender, the company said it bought 973,174 shares.

The company said that coupled with the shares it already owned, that represents the maximum number of shares it can purchase without triggering Circon's poison pill. The company had previously bought 1,000,100 shares.

The company said that if Circon still refuses to discuss a merger, it will begin a new tender offer to buy all outstanding common shares of Circon at $16.50 per share. At that price, it has a price/earnings ratio over 180 times trailing 12 months earnings.
The company also said it is considering a proxy contest to nominate two independent directors to Circon's board.

Connecticut-based U.S. Surgical launched an $18-per-share offer for Circon last August, then cut the bid to $17 in December. In June, it cut the bid again, to $14.50 a share, complaining of ppor earnings performance by Circon in 1997's first quarter.
Circon, a supplier of minimally invasive urological and gynocological surgery products, earned $0.06 a share in the first quarter compared to $0.13 a year earlier.
